build: Thalamus's two-sided disk release, G64 images of side A (SHA-256 4544cf5d…) and side B (b30bb735…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection; the title says 1990, the collection 1991 (orientation.md)

comments.text: Characters $00-$4E of chamber 1's character set ($5800-$5A77): the chamber's screen_map uses 62 of these 79, $30 most often (22 cells); all multicolour by its char_colours.

Character $4F of the chamber's character set ($5800-$5FFF), and the seven after it. The label is the engine's: wipe_char_set redefines character $4F here for a screen wipe; the chamber never calls it.
Characters $57-$7F of chamber 1's character set ($5AB8-$5BFF): the chamber's screen_map uses 31 of these 41, $6C most often (9 cells); all multicolour by its char_colours.
Characters $80-$83 of chamber 1's character set ($5C00-$5C1F): the chamber's screen_map uses 3 of these 4, $81 most often (3 cells); all multicolour by its char_colours.

Character $84 of the chamber's character set ($5C20-$5C27): one of the jack's column characters. jack_rise (from $877B) rotates its eight rows by one each time the jack rises a pixel row while the second pattern is drawn, so the screw thread appears to turn.
Rows 1-7 of character $84, moved up a row by jack_rise's rotation ($8780).
Row 7 of character $84, where jack_rise puts the row it took from the top ($878B).
Character $87 ($5C38-$5C3F), the other turning column character: rotated like $5C20 while the jack's third pattern is drawn ($878F).
Rows 1-7 of character $87, moved up a row by jack_rise ($8794).
Row 7 of character $87, where jack_rise puts the row it took from the top ($879F). The characters after it follow.

Characters $8F-$FF of chamber 1's character set ($5C7F-$5FFF, character $8F from its row 7): the chamber's screen_map uses 77 of these 113, $FF most often (276 cells); 103 multicolour by its char_colours.
Sprite block $80 of chamber 1's sprites ($6000-$603F). $80 is named by no animation script or routine found.

Sprite block $81 (the bank's sprites start at $6000, block $80), the panel's weapon icon: weapon_icon_draw copies the icon's second half into its first 24 bytes (loader_hand_over shows weapon 0's icon in a chamber).
Sprite block $82, where weapon_icon_draw copies the weapon icon's first half (24 bytes).
Sprite block $83 of chamber 1's sprites ($60C0-$60E6): $83 one of the panel's weapon icon blocks, which the engine's weapon_icon_draw draws into.
Sprite block $83 from row 13 ($60C0 plus 39), where weapon_icon_draw copies the icon's second half again (24 bytes).
Sprite block $84 from row 13, where weapon_icon_draw copies the icon's first half again.

Sprite blocks $85-$8F of chamber 1's sprites ($6167-$63FF, block $85 from its byte 39): $85-$86 the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames); $87 the chainsaw on its bench (demon_pump, saw_frames); $88 the bomb; $89 the boulder; $8A the rock under the top ledge, whole (overhang_frames); $8B-$8F the rock breaking up as the bomb hits it (overhang_frames).

Sprite blocks $90-$9F of chamber 1's sprites ($6400-$67FF): $90 the rock breaking up as the bomb hits it (overhang_frames); $91-$93 the lit fuse's sparks (spark_frames); $94 Chip on the jack; $95 the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames); $96 Chip struggling, which sawing swaps with $94; $97-$9B the jack's pump handle (handle_frames); $9C-$9F the purple demon's left and right halves pumping (pump_frames_a, pump_frames_b).

Sprite blocks $A0-$AF of chamber 1's sprites ($6800-$6BFF): $A0-$A5 the purple demon's left and right halves pumping (pump_frames_a, pump_frames_b); $A6-$A7 the purple demon watching once he stops; $A8-$A9 the purple demon when the cannon has fired; $AA-$AB the purple demon blown away; $AC-$AF the cannon's smoke puff (puff_frames).

Sprite blocks $B0-$BF of chamber 1's sprites ($6C00-$6FFF): $B0 the cannon's smoke puff (puff_frames); $B1 the green ball creature; $B2 the green ball at rest after rolling (ball_roll); $B3-$BA the green ball rolling; $BB the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames); $BC the chainsaw against him (saw_frames); $BD the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames); $BE the chainsaw against him (saw_frames); $BF the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames).

Sprite blocks $C0-$CF of chamber 1's sprites ($7000-$73FF): $C0 the chainsaw against him (saw_frames); $C1 the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames); $C2 the chainsaw against him (saw_frames); $C3 the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames); $C4-$C6 the chainsaw running (sawing cycles them); $C7-$C9 the chainsaw (saw_frames, values 0, 9 and 10); $CA the chainsaw demon at the start; $CB the chainsaw demon standing (sawdemon_script); $CC-$CF the smoke after the sawing (smoke_frames_t).

Sprite blocks $D0-$DF of chamber 1's sprites ($7400-$77FF): $D0-$D3 the smoke after the sawing (smoke_frames_t); $D4-$D7 the chainsaw demon walking right (sawdemon_script); $D8-$DB the chainsaw demon walking back left with the chainsaw; $DC-$DF the big worm's left and right halves, opening (worm_frames_a, worm_frames_b).

Sprite blocks $E0-$EF of chamber 1's sprites ($7800-$7BFF): $E0-$E1 the big worm's left and right halves, opening (worm_frames_a, worm_frames_b); $E2-$E3 the chainsaw demon sawing (sawdemon_frames); $E4 the chainsaw's glint (glint); $E5-$EF the blood (blood_frames).

Sprite blocks $F0-$FF of chamber 1's sprites ($7C00-$7FFE): $F0-$FB the explosion of the big worm and the green ball (burst_frames); $FC the small worm crawling (wormlet_frames); $FE the small worm crawling (wormlet_frames); $FF the chainsaw's glint, the other frame glint shows; and $FD is named by no animation script or routine found.
The last byte of the VIC bank at $4000-$7FFF, which the VIC shows in the open border while idle: torture_start sets it to $FF and the rescue screen and torture_leave set 0 and $FF.

Cold and warm start vectors for the KERNAL's cartridge test, both $AF6A (memory_wipe), followed at $8004 by the signature CBM80 ($C3 $C2 $CD $38 $30). Every level and chamber file carries them: a reset runs memory_wipe and erases the game (tested with a VICE reset from this chamber, which stopped at $AF6A); RESTORE did not reach it (VICE's RESTORE with the same checkpoint).

The chamber's 15 objects' starting x and y (30 bytes), copied to obj_xy by torture_start: 0 the rock under the top ledge (120,82), 1 the boulder, 2 and 3 the big worm, 4 the small worm, 5 the jack's top with Chip tied to it (276,160), 6 spare (the falling boulder, then smoke and blood), 7 the bomb on the seesaw, 8 a black sprite that rides up with the jack (glint) and later becomes the chainsaw, 9 the chainsaw demon (304,109), 10 the cannon's fuse, 11 the green ball creature, 12 and 13 the purple demon at the jack's pump, 14 the pump handle.

The 15 objects' starting sprite frames, copied to obj_frame: $8A the rock, $89 the boulder, $DC/$DD the worm, $FC the small worm, $94 Chip on the jack, $0F (blank) for 6 and 10, $88 the bomb, $E4 for object 8, $CA the chainsaw demon, $B1 the green ball, $A4/$A5 the pumping demon, $9B the handle.
The 15 objects' starting colours, copied to obj_colour.
The chamber's entry point: loader_hand_over jumps here once a torture chamber's file is in (part digit "3"), and the JMP goes on to torture_begin.

Set (at $8DF9) once the cannon's shot has carried the purple demon off the right of the screen while the chainsaw demon has not started: the main loop then counts rescue_delay down and goes to the rescue screen.
RUN/STOP pause: set when RUN/STOP is pressed with the joystick still; the loop then skips Clyde and the objects until the joystick moves. $8056 is not used.
Set by sawing ($90FA) when the chainsaw demon's script ends: Chip is cut in two and the main loop takes a life.
Frames between the jack's steps: jack_rise raises it a pixel when this runs out and starts it again at $37 (56 frames a pixel).
How many character rows the jack's column has grown by (jack_rise); jack_pattern turns it into the pattern drawn.
Set by demon_pump once the cannon has turned and its fuse has burnt down to line $C1 (or stands at $B8): the purple demon stops pumping, so the jack stops rising, and turns to watch.
Set by fuse_sparks when the cannon's shot reaches x $CC before the chainsaw demon has started: objects 12 and 13 then move with the shot.
Frames between the cannon's turning steps (cannon_turn, every sixth frame).
The purple demon's pump frame, 7 down to 0 (demon_pump), indexing pump_frames_a, pump_frames_b and handle_frames.
Frames between the demon's pump steps (every seventh frame).
Set to 3 by boulder_hit when the falling boulder reaches the seesaw: the loop then runs seesaw_and_bomb and overhang_crumble every frame.
The rock under the top ledge's frame index in overhang_frames: 0 whole; set to 7 when the bomb's flight reaches it, then counted down every other frame to 1, the blank frame.
Set to $32 when the bomb lands ($89CF); counted down each frame, and from $24 down the cannon turns (cannon_turn).
Set by boulder_hit when the shots have pushed the boulder left past x $53: it falls (boulder_hit's second half) and the green ball can no longer be shot.
Which spark frame the lit fuse shows (2 down to 0, fuse_sparks).
Frames before the fuse starts to burn down: set to $50 when the bomb lands; at 1 the loop calls fuse_burn every frame.
Frames between fuse_burn's steps ($1E).
Set by fuse_burn when the fuse has burnt down (six steps): with the fuse lit, fuse_sparks then fires the bomb across the screen.

Set to 7 by demon_pump when the jack reaches the top (Chip at line $78): the chainsaw demon comes out (smoke_and_blood, sawdemon_rev, sawing), the boulder cannot be pushed and the shot no longer carries the demon away.
Set with boulder_falling and cleared when the bomb lands: while set and the saw has started, the second band leaves object 6 alone.
Frames between the blood frames (smoke_and_blood, every fifth frame).
Frames between the smoke frames (every fourth frame).
The smoke's frame index, 12 down to 0 (smoke_frames).
Set by ball_hit at the green ball's first hit: ball_roll then rolls it right and back; cleared when it is home.
0 while the green ball rolls right; $32 when it reaches x $D7, counted down while it waits, and at 1 it rolls back left.
Frames between the rolling ball's frames (every fourth frame).
Set to $0C by worm_hit on the big worm's 36th hit, when worm_hits, counted down from 35, would go below zero: its two halves explode (the main loop at $8370) and it is no longer tested.
Set by ball_hit on the green ball's 51st hit, when ball_hits, counted down from 50, would go below zero: it explodes ($8353).
Frames the big worm shows white after a hit (2, raster_objects_a).
Frames the green ball shows white after a hit (raster_ball).
The big worm's explosion frame index, $0C down to 0 (burst_frames).
The green ball's explosion frame index.
Frames between explosion frames (every fifth), shared by both explosions.
0 while smoke_and_blood shows the smoke, 1 once it shows the blood (set at $8EA2); it also picks smoke_x, smoke_y, smoke_frames, smoke_colours and smoke_size.
Frames between the chainsaw demon's revving steps (every fifth frame).
The chainsaw demon's place in sawdemon_script.
Set when sawdemon_script reaches a 0: the demon walks, a pixel a frame.
Set when sawdemon_script reaches a 1: the demon (with the chainsaw) walks left instead of right.
Set when the demon walking left reaches x $30 (304): the loop runs sawing instead of sawdemon_rev.
The read position in saw_script.
Frames left of the current saw_script step, from saw_times.
Frames between the big worm's frames (every sixth).
The small worm's read position in wormlet_dx, moved on every fourth frame.
Frames between the small worm's frames (every third).
The small worm's read position in wormlet_frames.
Set when the small worm reaches the end of its crawl while the big worm is dying: worms is no longer called.
Set by fuse_touch when a full-charge flame (fire held for 36 frames) touches the fuse: the loop then runs fuse_sparks every frame, and the cannon fires when the fuse has burnt down.
Set by cannon_turn when the cannon has turned with the fuse unlit: bomb_roll rolls the bomb out of it.
Frames between Chip's struggling frames during the sawing (every third frame).
glint's count: 256 frames between showings.
glint's step, $14 down to 0, indexing glint_colours.
bomb_roll's read position in bomb_roll_x and bomb_roll_y.
The cannon's turning frames left, 3 at the start (cannon_turn).
The seesaw's tipping frames left, 4 at the start (seesaw_and_bomb).
The fuse's burning steps left, 6 (fuse_burn).
The cannon's smoke puff frame index, $0B down to 0 (puff_frames).
The big worm's hits left before the last: $23 (35) at the start. worm_hit stores it less one while that stays 0 or more, so the worm bursts on its 36th hit.
The green ball's hits left before the last: $32 (50) at the start. ball_hit stores it less one while that stays 0 or more, so the ball bursts on its 51st hit.
Frames between the end of the smoke and the first blood frame: $78 (120), counted down by smoke_and_blood once blood_phase is set.
Frames before the smoke starts: $CD (205).
The smoke's colours left, 3 (smoke_colours).
The big worm's frame index in worm_frames_a/b, 8 down to 0.
The blood's frame index in blood_frames: from $0A down once, then from 5.
$FF while idle; bomb_roll sets $64 (100) when the bomb has rolled out of the unlit cannon, and when the count runs out the chamber starts again ($83CE) without taking a life.
An explosion's frames, read from the end: $F0-$FB, then $0F (blank) at index 0; used for the big worm's halves and the green ball.
The boulder's fall steps left, $0C at the start, indexing boulder_dy.
The pixels the boulder drops at each fall step (read from the end, 1 up to 6, so it speeds up); at step 3 it hits the seesaw.
The starting ninth x bits for obj_x_msb: objects 5, 8 and 9 ($C8 in the second byte) are past x 255.
The starting multicolour bits for sprite_mc_bands, a byte per band.
The starting background-priority bits for sprite_behind_bands: none behind.

Sets the chamber up (also after a lost life, from retry_screen): clears the variables $8054-$8088, copies the screen from screen_map ($95DC) into the screen at $4400 with each character's colour from char_colours, sets the engine for a chamber ($126C, $1216, shot_y_max $CF, Clyde's dying count $ED, player_x_min $18 and limit $41, object_collisions' slot 15 through $12DE, $12E6 and $12EA), the variables' starting values, the colours, Clyde at (189,205), the 15 objects from objects_start_xy, objects_start_frames and objects_start_colours; starts the tune and the raster chain at raster_panel.

Operand of the LDX at $8131: the screen copy's page count (3 down to 0, stored at $8119). The rest of torture_start: shot_y_max $CF, Clyde's dying count $1288 = $ED, $12EA = $F8, $120C, $126C (torture chamber) and $1216 set, $12E6 = 3, the jack's screen address $469F, the counts and scripts the puzzle starts from, the colours ($D021 $0E), player_x_min $18, the objects, Clyde's sprite, and the raster chain.

The chamber's main loop, once a frame: RUN/STOP pause, the weapons tablet or Clyde (player_control, player_fire, player_animate, panel_anim), then the puzzle's routines (fuse_burn, fuse_sparks, jack_rise, the saw sequence or glint, boulder_hit, worms, bomb_roll, cannon_turn, seesaw_and_bomb, demon_pump, ball_roll and the explosions), player_dead or the collision tests, the music, and the end: restart_count, chip_sawn or Clyde's death take a life (lives below zero is game over), rescued leads to the rescue screen.
Frames from rescued to the rescue screen: $30, counted down by the main loop unless Clyde is dying.
Starts the chamber's tune (torture_tune at $9AC4); the main loop calls it again whenever the tune has ended.
Object 6's x in the saw sequence, by blood_phase: $22 for the smoke, $08 for the blood (both past x 255).
Object 6's y by blood_phase: $58, $5B.
Object 6's frame by blood_phase: the smoke's (written from smoke_frames_t by smoke_and_blood) and, at $83F8, the blood's.
The blood's current frame, written from blood_frames by smoke_and_blood.
Object 6's colour by blood_phase: the smoke's (from smoke_colours_t), then red ($02) for the blood.
Object 6's double width and height by blood_phase: none for the smoke, $10 (sprite 4) for the blood.

Raster routine at the top of the screen (line 0): sprites_band1 puts objects 0-4 on sprites 3-7; Clyde's and the shots' pointers are blanked for this band; sprites 1 and 2 are double width while Clyde is dying (the speech bubble); while seesaw_hit is set sprite 5 shows object 7, the bomb in flight, in place of object 2; object 4's colour flips bit 2 every frame (the small worm flickers); the big worm's halves (sprites 5 and 6) are light red or black while they explode, white while worm_flash counts, otherwise object 2's colour. Then clyde_sprites, and next raster_objects_b at line $53.
Raster routine at line $53: objects 6-9 on sprites 4-7.

Operand of the ORA at $8477: the second band's ninth x bits (sprite_msb_bands' second byte AND $F0), written at $846F. Then each of objects 6-9 gets its colour, position (obj_sprite_xy) and frame on sprites 4-7.

Operand of the ORA at $84AA: the second band's multicolour bits ($C001 AND $F0). Then the band's priority bits (without sprite 3's). Before the saw starts sprite 6 (object 8) is double width, and while the boulder falls object 6 is drawn as the boulder (object 1's position, frame $89, colour 8). Once the saw has started, unless sprite6_boulder is set, object 6 is the smoke or the blood: position, frame, colour and size from smoke_x, smoke_y, smoke_frames, smoke_colours and smoke_size by blood_phase, past x 255 and single-colour. Next raster_jack at line $69.
Raster routine at line $69: sprite 3 shows object 5 (Chip on the jack's top): past x 255, its colour, saved position and frame, multicoloured. Next raster_ball at line $90.

Raster routine at line $90: sprite 4 shows object 11 (the green ball, later the bomb) at its current position, with its frame; colour light red or black while it explodes, white while ball_flash counts, otherwise its own.
Operand of the ORA at $85A5: object 11's ninth x bit (bit 4 of obj_x_msb's third byte), written at $859D. Then its multicolour bit.

Operand of the ORA at $85B7: object 11's multicolour bit (bit 4 of sprite_mc_bands' third byte). Then $10 (sprite 4) while the green ball explodes and the boulder has not fallen, else 0, into the ORA at $85D4.
Operand of the ORA at $85D4: sprite 4's bit while the green ball explodes, ORed into $862E, the double height raster_objects_c sets, so the explosion is drawn tall. Next raster_objects_c at line $B0.
Raster routine at line $B0: objects 12-14 (the purple demon's two halves and the pump handle) on sprites 5-7, and object 10 on sprite 3.
Operand of the ORA at $85ED: the third band's ninth x bits ($C00C AND $E0), written at $85E5. Then objects 12-14's colours and positions onto sprites 5-7.

Low byte of the LDA $C176,X at $8608, objects 12-14's frames, which the loop stores in sprites 5-7's pointers; the label is the engine's (scroll_draw_column reads the levels' tile table at $8609), and a chamber never scrolls.
Operand of the ORA at $8620: the third band's multicolour bits ($C002 AND $E0). Then its priority bits.

Operand of the LDA at $862D, this band's double height ($D017): $60 for sprites 5 and 6 (the purple demon), $68 once the cannon has fired, with sprite 4's bit added by raster_ball while the green ball explodes. Once the cannon has fired, object 10 becomes the cannon's smoke: at ($50,$C4), colour $0A, its frame from the operand at $8642.
Operand of the LDA at $8641: the cannon smoke's frame, written by fuse_sparks from puff_frames. Then sprite 3's ninth x bit is cleared and the operand at $865B ORed in.

Operand of the ORA at $865A: $10 once the cannon's shot has passed x 255 (fuse_sparks, $8DB7), which keeps sprite 4's ninth x bit set for the rest of the screen; fuse_sparks also tests it as the shot's high bit. Then sprite 3 shows object 10 (the fuse, or the smoke): colour, position and frame.
Operand of the ORA at $8684: sprite 3's multicolour bit (bit 3 of $C002). Then only sprites 1 and 2 keep double width. Next raster_panel at line $E1.

Raster routine at line $E1 (and the chain's first, at line $F9, where irq_install starts it): no priority or double height, the score panel's sprites (panel_sprites, or panel_sprites_tablet while the tablet is up), and frame_divider. Next raster_panel_lower at line $F4.
Raster routine at line $F4: panel_lower (after two NOPs for timing) and on to raster_border; while the tablet is up, nothing until raster_border at line $F9.
The bottom border: raster_open_border, Clyde's colour back to light red ($0A) except while a flame charge is building, and one added to the frame flag $120D. Next raster_objects_a at line 0.
Low byte of the screen address of the jack column's top row: $9F at the start ($469F), moved up a row ($28) by jack_rise each time the column grows.
High byte of the jack column's screen address ($46 at the start).
The jack column's first character for each of jack_pattern's three patterns: $80, $83, $FE.
The column's second character by pattern: $81, $84, $87.
The column's third character by pattern: $82, $85, $88.
The column's fourth character by pattern: $86, $FE, $FE.

The jack rises while the purple demon pumps: unless demon_stopped, every 56 frames (jack_delay) and while Chip (object 5) is at line $78 or below, Chip and object 8 move up a pixel; when Chip's y AND 7 is 5 the column grows a character row above the last, four characters of jack_pattern's pattern with their colours from char_colours; every step turns the screw by rotating character $84 (second pattern) or $87 (third) a row. From line $A0 to $77 that is 41 steps, about 46 seconds at 50 frames a second.
Operand of the LDA at $8708, $37: the frames between the jack's steps less one. The label is the engine's (scroll_column reads the levels' row pointers at $8709/$870A).
The STA that restarts jack_delay (the label is the engine's, as $8709's). Then: nothing while Chip is above line $78; otherwise object 8 moves up a pixel.

Low byte of the DEC $C270 at $8714 (object 8's y). The label is the engine's (scroll_column and get_ready_strip read the levels' first map row at $8715). The rest of jack_rise: Chip up a pixel; on every eighth line the new row (jack_screen up $28, jack_rows plus one, four characters from jack_chars_0-3 by jack_pattern, their colours from char_colours into colour RAM $94 pages higher); then the screw turns.
A second RTS, which nothing reaches.
The jack column's pattern from jack_rows: X = 0 before the first row, 1 for one to three rows, 2 from four.
Low bytes of the cannon's three character frames, read by cannon_frames as it counts 2, 1, 0: $87E8, $87D4, $87C0.
High bytes of the cannon's frames, all $87. The frames follow it: $87C0, $87D4 and $87E8, each four rows of five characters for rows 18-21, columns 2-6 of the screen.
Inside the cannon's frames (the second byte of the frame at $87D4); the label is the engine's (get_ready_strip reads the levels' second map row at $87D5).
The fuse's x (object 10) after each cannon frame, by cannon_frames: $30, $23, $1F (the turn runs 2, 1, 0, so $1F first).
The fuse's y after each cannon frame: $BC, $C2, $C5.

Turns the cannon once the bomb is in it (called while cannon_wait is below $24): every sixth frame draws the next of three character frames into rows 18-21, columns 2-6 and moves the fuse (object 10) with it. After the third: nothing more if the fuse is lit; otherwise bomb_rolling, and the bomb rolls back out.
Low byte of the LDA at $882A: the cannon frame's address, from cannon_src_lo, moved on five bytes a row.

High byte of the cannon frame's address (cannon_src_hi), carried into at $883F. Then the screen offset moves on a row ($2D, 40 plus the five drawn) and the fuse takes this frame's position from fuse_x and fuse_y.
Operand of the LDX at $8856: the rows left to draw (3 down to 0, written at $8825).
The fuse burns down once the bomb is in the cannon (called every frame once fuse_wait reaches 1): every 31 frames object 10 moves down a pixel, six times; then cannon_fired is set.
Low bytes of the seesaw's four character frames, read by seesaw_frames as it counts 3 to 0: $8888, $88B5, $88E2, $890F.
High bytes of the seesaw's frames: $89 for index 0, $88 for 1-3. The frames follow from $8888, each five rows of nine characters for rows 6-10, columns 1-9.
Inside the seesaw's first frame (from $8888); the label is the engine's (get_ready_strip reads the levels' third map row at $8895).
The seesaw's second frame (index 2, drawn after $8888), five rows of nine characters.
The seesaw's third frame (index 1), five rows of nine characters.
The seesaw's last frame (index 0), five rows of nine characters.

Runs every frame once the boulder has hit the seesaw. While seesaw_frames lasts it draws the seesaw's next frame (four in all) into the screen at $44F1. Then it moves the bomb by its two scripts, a byte each a frame: bomb_x_script (below $80 right by the low nibble, $80 and up left by it, $FF the end) and bomb_y_script (the same downwards and upwards, with $FE breaking the rock under the top ledge and $FD starting the cannon). When object 7 falls past line $9E the bomb moves to object 11 and object 7 becomes the boulder again.
From here a seesaw row is drawn (the label is the engine's: get_ready_strip reads the levels' fourth map row at $8955): nine characters from the frame to the screen.
Low byte of the LDA at $895A, the seesaw frame's address, moved on nine bytes a row.
High byte of the seesaw frame's address. Then the screen offset moves on a row ($31, 40 plus nine).
Operand of the LDX at $8977: the rows left to draw (4 down to 0).
Operand of the LDY at $897C: which object the bomb's scripts move, as an offset from object 7 in obj_xy: 0, then 8 (object 11) after the swap at $8A3B; torture_start clears it.
Low byte of the bomb's x script pointer (bomb_x_script, $8A4E at the start), moved on a byte at each read.
High byte of the bomb's x script pointer. A byte below $80 adds its low nibble to the x; one from $80 subtracts it (through the SBC operand at $89AB); $FF stops the x steps.
Operand of the SBC at $89AA: a leftward step's size, the script byte's low nibble.
Low byte of the bomb's y script pointer (bomb_y_script, $8ABB at the start), moved on by bomb_y_next.

High byte of the y script pointer. $FE breaks the rock under the top ledge (overhang_frame 7, screen cells $44AC-$44AE blanked); $FD starts the cannon (cannon_wait $32, fuse_wait $50) and clears sprite6_boulder; both are followed at once by the next byte. $FF stops; anything else is a step, down below $80 and up from $80.
Operand of the SBC at $89FE: an upward step's size. Then the swap test: once object 7's y is $9E or more, the bomb becomes object 11.

The swap (the label is the engine's: get_ready_strip reads the levels' fifth map row at $8A15): object 11 takes object 7's position and the bomb's frame $88 in black, object 7 takes the boulder's frame $89 in orange at object 1's position (and saved sprite position), and the scripts move object 11 from now on.
Moves the bomb's y script pointer on a byte.
The bomb's x steps, a byte a frame (see $8980): right fast, slowing to nothing, then left, ending with $FF at $8ABA.

The bomb's y steps, a byte a frame (see $89B1): up fast and slowing, down, $FE where it meets the rock under the top ledge ($8AD9), then bounces lower and lower down into the cannon, ending with a drop of 13, $FD and $FF ($8B29).
Inside bomb_y_script, four bytes before its $FE; the label is the engine's (get_ready_strip reads the levels' sixth map row at $8AD5).
bomb_y_script after the $FE: the bomb bounces lower and lower down into the cannon, ending with a drop of 13, $FD at $8B29 and $FF.
The rock under the top ledge's frames by overhang_frame: index 0 $8A (whole), then from index 7 down to 1 $8B to $90 as it breaks and $0F (gone).
Shows the rock's frame (object 0) from overhang_frames, stepping overhang_frame down every other frame from 7 to 1.
73 bytes nothing in the chamber reads, the same bytes as level 3.2's file holds at these addresses.
$B6, a level's end scroll position in the engine (scroll_column, object_kill and game_frame_music read it here); a chamber does not scroll, so nothing in it uses this byte.

$5B, the first character Clyde can pass through: the engine's movement and landing code compares the cells under and beside Clyde with it ($2CC4, $2D1A, $2D95, sfx_land, and $AD1A in player_dead), and that code runs in the chamber too, so characters below $5B are the chamber's floors and walls (the engine's tests treat a character as solid when it is below this one).
The dot-matrix sign's sprite colour on the rescue screen, set every frame by raster_rescue_top from matrix_colours ($A044); on a level the engine's level_colours_next reads its table here.
The dot-matrix sign's first sprite multicolour ($D025), set by raster_rescue_top from $A04C.
The dot-matrix sign's second sprite multicolour ($D026), set by raster_rescue_top from $A054.
raster_rescue_top's row counter for the sign: 5 at the top, counted down by raster_rescue_row as it moves the sprites down a row.
Object 12's frames (the purple demon's left half), indexed by pump_step: 0-7 the pump cycle, 8 watching once demon_stopped, 9 when the cannon has fired, 10 blown away.
Object 13's frames (the demon's right half), indexed like pump_frames_a.
Object 14's frames (the jack's pump handle), indexed like pump_frames_a: the handle rises and falls with the pump and stays put once the demon stops.
The last entry of handle_frames, $9A (the handle at rest, blown away). The label is the engine's: level_colours_next reads a level's table here.

The purple demon works the jack's pump. Once demon_stopped, it only shows frame 10 when blown away or 9 when the cannon has fired. Otherwise, until the saw has started, every seventh frame: if Chip (object 5) has risen above line $78, the chainsaw (object 8) is set at x $68 (its ninth bit stays set, so 360) and y $67 with frame $87 in light grey, the second band's multicolour bits become $F8, and saw_started is set; if not, pump_step moves on (7 down to 0) and at steps 2 and 4, when the cannon has turned (cannon_frames 0) and the fuse (object 10) is at line $B8 or past $C0, the demon stops (index 8). The three objects then take their frames from pump_frames_a, pump_frames_b and handle_frames.
The chainsaw's y ($67, one less than its x) and the rest of its start. The label is the engine's: level_colours_next reads a level's second colour table here.
The pump steps at which the demon checks the cannon (2 and 4). The label is the engine's: level_band_routines reads a level's routine table here.
From here the three objects' frames are copied from the tables. The label is the engine's: level_section_from_scroll reads a level's section table here.
Object 13's frame, from pump_frames_b. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
Object 14's frame, from handle_frames. The label is the engine's: stage_start reads a level's table here.
The stopped demon: blown away or not. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's strip length here.
The branch to frame 10, blown away. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
Frame 9 when the cannon has fired, else no change. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The chainsaw's glint colours, read from glint_step $14 down to 0: black, dark grey, grey, light grey, white held for 13 steps, then light grey, grey and dark grey.
glint_colours from its second entry. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
Six of glint_colours' white entries. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
glint_colours' last white entries and light grey. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
glint_colours' last two entries, grey and dark grey. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.

The chainsaw glints on its bench while it waits (called each frame until the saw starts): while object 8 is at line $6B or below, once every 256 frames (glint_wait) it runs 21 steps, one every fourth frame (when frame_divider's $1219 and $121A are both set), showing the frame in the LDA operand at $8C7A with the colours from glint_colours; after the last it blanks object 8 (frame $0F) and flips that operand between $FF and $E4 (EOR $1B), so that showings alternate between the two frames.
The chainsaw's height test, line $6B. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The 256-frame wait. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The frame_divider test, every fourth frame. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's spawn section table here.
The glint's step count. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's spawn section table here.
The end of the glint. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.

Operand of the LDA at $8C79: the glint frame shown on object 8, $FF or $E4, flipped at the end of each showing. The rest of glint stores it and the step's colour, and at the end resets the step to $15 and the wait.
The bomb's x steps as it rolls back out of the unlit cannon (bomb_roll): 4 pixels a frame slowing to 0, then $FF, the end.
The bomb's y steps, read with bomb_roll_x: down by the value, or up by the low seven bits when bit 7 is set ($81).

Rolls the bomb (object 11) out of the cannon when the cannon turned without the fuse lit (bomb_rolling): each frame the next steps from bomb_roll_x and bomb_roll_y. When x reaches $4C or the steps end, the bomb is drawn in front of the scenery again ($C005 = 0) and, the first time, restart_count is set to $64: 100 frames later the chamber starts again without taking a life.
High byte of bomb_roll_x's address in the LDA. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_icons reads a level's table here.
The JSR to the end of the roll at x $4C. The label is the engine's: timer_reset reads a level's table here.
The y step's BMI. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads the address of a level's per-frame routine here (level_frame_call).
Operand bytes of the y step's LDA. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_player_call address here.
An upward step goes to $8CF9. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_jump_call address here.
A downward step's size, the low seven bits. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_anim_call address here.
A downward step is added to the bomb's y. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_hook_call address here.
Inside the ADC. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's strip colour here.
Inside the ADC. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's second strip colour here.
The bomb's new y is stored. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's third strip colour here.
An upward step: its size goes into the SBC's operand at $8D03. The label is the engine's: the Get Ready strip code ($3B63) reads a level's table here.
Operand of the SBC at $8D02: an upward step's size. Then the read position moves on; the end of the roll (from $8D0B) puts the bomb in front and starts restart_count.

The handler for a shot on the boulder (object 1), and the boulder's fall, run each frame once boulder_falling is set. Before it falls, unless the saw has started, each hit spends the shot and pushes the boulder one pixel left; past x $53 it starts to fall (boulder_falling and sprite6_boulder). Falling, it drops by boulder_dy for $0C steps, faster as it goes, and at three steps from the end seesaw_hit is set; once the fall is over, until the cannon has fired, object 11 is drawn behind the scenery ($C005 = $10), so the bomb is hidden inside the cannon.
The handler's RTS. The label is the engine's: get_ready fills the screen with a level's character from here.
An RTS. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup reads a level's tune address, low byte, here.
The end of the fall: unless the cannon has fired. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup reads a level's tune address, high byte, here.
Operand of the LDA at $8D57. The label is the engine's: game_frame_music reads a level's end tune address, low byte, here.
The LDA's operand, high byte. The label is the engine's: game_frame_music reads a level's end tune address, high byte, here.

The branch past the cannon test and the store of $10 into the third band's background-priority bits. The label is the engine's: object_spawn and object_set_type read a level's animation script table (low bytes) here.
The lit fuse's sparks on object 10, cycled every frame by fuse_sparks.
The sparks once the fuse has burnt into the turned cannon (line $C2 or below): one spark frame in three, so they flicker.

Runs each frame once the fuse is lit. Before the cannon fires it cycles the spark frames on object 10. After, unless the chamber is won: the cannon's smoke puff steps through puff_frames every other frame; the bomb (object 11) flies right six pixels a frame, setting shot_past_255 when it wraps; with demon_blown_away the demon's halves (objects 12 and 13) move with it, their ninth x bits ($20, $40 of $C25D) set as they wrap. Before x 256, from x $4E the bomb is drawn in front of the scenery, and reaching x $CC before the saw has started blows the demon away. Past 256, at x $5A it sets rescued; if the saw has started the bomb is held there instead, and the chamber is never won.
The smoke puff's frame index, every other frame. The label is the engine's: object_spawn and object_set_type read a level's animation script table (high bytes) here.
The first demon half's ninth x bit. The label is the engine's: object_spawn and object_set_type read a level's third animation table here.
Operand of the SBC at $8E01: the bomb is held back six pixels while the saw runs. The label is the engine's: object_kill and object_spawn read a level's colour cycle table (low bytes) here.
The demon is blown away when the bomb reaches x $CC with the saw not started. The label is the engine's: object_kill and object_spawn read a level's colour cycle table (high bytes) here.
The cannon's smoke puff, read from $0B down to 0 by fuse_sparks into the operand at $8642: blank, then frames $AC-$B0 and back, blank again.
The puff's last frames, shrinking. The label is the engine's: object_kill reads a level's third colour cycle table here.

The blood's frames $EF to $E6, and $E5 at blood_frames + 10: smoke_and_blood starts at index $0A and runs down to 0, then loops from 5, so the first pass shows the whole flow and the loop the last six.
The blood's first frame, $E5. The label is the engine's: object_kill reads a level's death movement table (x) here.
The smoke's frames, read from index 12 down to 0: $CC to $D3 as it billows, then five blanks.
The smoke's colours for its three cycles, read from the end: light grey, grey, then dark grey.

Runs each frame once the saw has started, on object 6: after smoke_wait (205 frames), three cycles of smoke, a frame every fourth frame and darker each cycle; then blood_phase is set, and after blood_wait (120 frames) the blood runs, a frame every fifth frame, for as long as the chamber lasts.
The blood's frame step. The label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_path read a level's death movement table (y) here.
The smoke's wait. The label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_10 read a level's y movement script table (low bytes) here.
The smoke's next cycle and colour. The label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_10 read a level's y movement script table (high bytes) here.

The chainsaw demon's script, a byte every fifth frame (sawdemon_rev): 0 starts the walk, 1 turns him left, anything else is his frame. He shows frame $CB, walks right (frames $D7-$D4) to where demon_pump put the chainsaw, then turns and walks back left carrying it ($D8-$DB).
sawdemon_script's walk-right frames. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's hit point table here.
sawdemon_script's last walk-left frames. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's wake-delay table here.

The chainsaw demon (object 9) fetches the chainsaw, once the saw has started: every fifth frame it reads sawdemon_script; walking, he moves a pixel a frame, right, or left carrying the chainsaw (object 8); when he is back at x $30 (304) sawdemon_arrived is set and sawing takes over. He arrives after the script's last byte, so its DEC opcode ($CE, at $8ECA) is shown as his frame for a few frames.
The next script byte. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's table here.
A script byte of 0 starts the walk, 1 turns him left. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's hit threshold table here.
The walk: right or left. The label is the engine's: ride_parent reads a level's x offset table here.
Walking right, the demon's new x. The label is the engine's: ride_parent reads a level's y offset table here.
Walking left: one pixel less, down to x $30, the chainsaw moved with him. The label is the engine's: object_kill compares the slot of a level's end creature with this byte.
For each saw_script value (0-13), how far left of the chainsaw demon the chainsaw is drawn.
For each saw_script value, how far above the demon the chainsaw is drawn.
For each saw_script value, the chainsaw's frame (object 8).
saw_frames for value 6: the chainsaw shaking as it bites, written by sawing from saw_shake_frames.
saw_frames for value 7: the chainsaw running, cycled $C4-$C6 every other frame by sawing; then values 8-13.
For each saw_script value, the chainsaw demon's frame (object 9).

For each saw_script value, the step's length: the count runs from this value down past 0, so value + 1 frames. torture_start sets the first six to 2 at every try, and each $FD in the script takes one off them.
saw_times for value 7 ($14, set again by torture_start), cut by 8 at each $FD; then values 8-13.

The sawing, a value a step: each value places the chainsaw against the demon and picks both frames and the step's length. Values 0, 9 and 10 make Chip struggle; 12 and 13 set the chainsaw shaking (seen in value 6's frame). $FE goes back three values and plays them again, nine times over; $FD shortens the steps; $FF is the end: Chip is cut in two. Its four $FE loops and two $FD make up most of the 224 bytes.
Written with each saw_script value at $9100; nothing reads it.
The chainsaw's shake count: $12 when a value of 12 or more starts, counted down every other frame as saw_shake_frames go into saw_frames' value 6.
saw_script's repeat count for $FE: torture_start sets $9F, so the first $FE sets 8; each $FE goes back while the count runs down past 0, nine repeats, and then reads on, leaving $FF for the next $FE.
The chainsaw's frames while it shakes, read from the end by sawing.

The chainsaw demon saws Chip in two, once he has arrived (each frame): every other frame the running saw frame cycles and a shake steps on; when the step's time runs out the next saw_script value is read. Values 0, 9 and 10 make Chip (object 5) struggle, flipping his frame every third frame (0 also turns the chainsaw light red), others show him still ($94); $FE and $FD are as saw_script says; at $FF it stays there and adds one to chip_sawn every frame, which takes the life. Each value places the chainsaw against the demon (saw_dx, saw_dy) and sets both frames and the step's length.
Operand of the LDX at $90FE, the value just read, restored after the $FD test. Then the shake starts for values $0C and up, and the chainsaw is placed and both frames set.
The big worm's left half (object 2), read from worm_frame 8 down to 0 every sixth frame: it opens to frame $E0 and closes again as it lets the small worm out.
The big worm's right half (object 3), read with worm_frames_a.
The small worm's x steps, one every fourth frame: twelve of 1, nine of 0, then 1, 2, 3 and nine of 4; $FF ends the crawl. The steps add up to 54, so it never passes x 255.
The small worm's crawling frames ($FC-$FE), one every third frame.

The big worm and the small worm (each frame until wormlet_stopped): the big worm's halves step through worm_frames_a/b every sixth frame unless it is dying; the small worm (object 4) crawls by wormlet_dx and animates by wormlet_frames; at the end of its crawl it starts again at x $80 and the big worm opens once more, or, once the big worm is dying, wormlet_stopped is set and it stays.

The green ball (object 11) rolls once it has been shot (ball_rolling): right a pixel a frame to x $D7, its frame stepping through $B3-$BA every fourth frame; it rests $32 frames, then rolls left to x $74 and stops, frame $B2.

The rescue screen's dot-matrix sign, a byte for each of its seven rows (the top at $92B3): each bit shows one of the eight sprites in that row, each a little picture of Clyde's face (block $4E). matrix_scroll fills it a letter at a time from matrix_font.
The sign's top row (matrix_rows + 6), which raster_rescue_top shows.
" CLYDE HAS SAVED CHIP FROM" and $FF: print_at's string 5, the first line of the rescue story.
"BEING SLICED IN TWO" and $FF, string 6.
"CHIP OFFERS CLYDE HIS COLLECTION" and $FF, string 7.
"OF MAGIC POTION CREATURES AS REWARD" and $FF, string 8.
"WITHOUT HESITATION CLYDE ACCEPTS THEM" and $FF, string 9.
"THEN CONTINUES ON HIS QUEST" and $FF, string 10.
"RESCUE CHIP AS SOON AS POSSIBLE" and $FF, string 11: the Get Ready screen's line.

Undoes torture_start's engine settings on the way out: panel and tablet sprites back to y $DD, $126C cleared, $24F0 and $7FFF set to $FF, object_collisions' slot settings back ($12DE 0, $12E6 0, $12EA 8), player_x_min $1F, player_x_limit's second byte (past 255) back to $3B and shot_y_max $BF.

Puts Clyde (sprite 0) and his two shot sprites (1 and 2) on the VIC: positions, pointers, colours and ninth x bits, with $D026 (the sprites' second multicolour) yellow, and enables all eight sprites; raster_objects_a calls it each frame.

Clyde's collision tests (each frame unless he is dying): the handler is $94A6, which jumps into player_hurt past its invulnerability checks, so touching kills him whatever. Tested against Clyde's box: object 3 (the big worm), object 7 (the bomb on the seesaw, the boulder after the swap), object 4 (the small worm, with the first band's high and tall bits masked by $7F) and object 11 (the green ball, later the bomb).
Tests object 3 against Clyde (A = 0) or the shot (A = 1, through the operand at $952A), skipping it when it shows the blank frame $0F or frames $F0-$FB.
Tests object 11 the same way, skipping frames $0F and $F0-$FB.
The handler for a shot on the fuse: only a full charge (the flame, $1236 at $24 or more) lights it (fuse_lit).
clyde_touch's handler: a JMP to $3CEC in player_hurt, past its invulnerability tests.

Shot X's collision tests (each frame for both shots, unless there is none): the big worm (object 3, handler worm_hit), the green ball (object 11, ball_hit) while the boulder has not fallen, the boulder (object 1, boulder_hit), and, until the cannon has fired, the fuse (object 10, fuse_touch), tested at its position with frame $FF so it is never skipped.
An unreferenced JMP test_object.

Puts the object under test (A = x, X = y, Y = frame) in the spare slot 15 ($C27D, $C27E, $C179), which is the only one object_collisions tests in a chamber, and sets the box: Clyde's, or shot $43's when the operand at $952A is set.
Operand of the LDA at $9529: 0 to test against Clyde's box, 1 against the shot's. Then Clyde's box (player_box_x, player_box_y), or from $9538 the shot's (shot_box, shot_box_y).
Runs object_collisions for slot 15 with its ninth x bit and its tall bit clear.
The same with A masking the ninth x bits in X and the tall bits in Y, written into slot 15's band ($C25E, $C009) through the AND operands at $955C and $9562.
Operand of the AND at $955B: the mask for the ninth x bits.
Operand of the AND at $9561: the mask for the tall bits. Then object_collisions.

The handler for a shot on the big worm: unless it is dying, the shot is spent and worm_hits counts down with a white flash (worm_flash); after its last hit the worm bursts (worm_dying, worm_burst), its halves blank, and score value 10 is added (four in the tens digit, through score_add at $B80C).

The handler for a shot on the green ball: the shot is spent, the first hit starts it rolling, each hit flashes it white; after its last hit it bursts (ball_dying), $15 higher, and score value 7 is added (one in the tens digit).
Nothing calls this: a DEC of the border colour and an RTS.

The chamber's screen, 40 by 25 characters, copied to the screen at $4400 by torture_start with each character's colour from char_colours. The copy runs four whole pages, so it also takes 24 bytes past the map (from char_colours) into $47E8-$47FF.
Each of the 256 characters' colour in the colour RAM, looked up by torture_start as it copies screen_map.
The chamber's tune, in the music driver's format (header and three voice streams with their sections, to $9CD8); tune_start plays it.
Clears the screen (screen_fill with 0) and sets 40 columns.
memory_swap 6: exchanges the text character set with the chamber's, for the Get Ready and rescue screens.
The chamber's first start: weapon_setup with X = 0 and Y = 0 (weapon 0 at grade 0, the panel's icon set by loader_hand_over), then retry_screen.

The Get Ready screen before each try: clears the engine's variables $120C-$126C and sets $126D-$1272 to $FF, swaps in the text characters, draws the lives digit and GET READY, moves the panel and tablet sprites down to y $ED, points print_at's strings 5-11 at this file's texts and prints string 11, "RESCUE CHIP AS SOON AS POSSIBLE", at $4684, starts sound effects $15 and $16, and runs the colour bars (raster_retry_bars). Fire silences it, blanks the screen, swaps the characters back and starts the chamber (torture_start).

The colour bars' sixteen colours, read from the end, so from the top down: brown, red, orange, light red, light grey, yellow twice, white, light green, cyan, green, light blue twice, purple, dark grey and blue.
A second copy of retry_bars_a; raster_retry_bars takes one or the other on alternate frames, so the bars do not change.
Low bytes of retry_bars_a and retry_bars_b, picked by frame_divider's $1219.
High bytes of the two colour lists.

The Get Ready screen's raster routine at line $69 (line $F9 the first time, where irq_install starts the chain): sixteen lines of background colour from the list for this frame (delays from colour_bar_delays); then the background and the second sprite multicolour yellow, and the lives sprite (sprite 0, block $4E, Clyde's face, light red, at x $114, y $98), shown or hidden with frame_divider's $121B so it blinks every four frames. Next raster_retry_panel at line $E0.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $9DF0, the colour list's address, from retry_bars_lo.
High byte of the colour list's address, from retry_bars_hi. The code after it writes the bars and sets the lives sprite.
The Get Ready screen's line $E0: panel_sprites. Next raster_retry_lower at line $F4.
The Get Ready screen's line $F4: panel_lower and the open border. Next raster_retry_bars at line $69.
Low bytes of the seven texts at $92B4-$936A, copied into print_at's strings 5-11.
High bytes of the seven texts.

The rescue: plays rescue_tune and shows the dot-matrix sign spelling WELL DONE, its dots little pictures of Clyde's face. Every other frame two colour lists rotate a place: the big letters take the first list's front colour and the six story lines take successive places of the second, so the colours ripple down them. After $78 counts every other frame (about five seconds) it prints WELL DONE in big letters, the six lines of story and the potion digit 6; potion_award then counts the digit down, paying potions. Fire leaves (torture_exit).
Prints big string 14, the potion digit at $ABF3, at $470B.
Leaves the rescue screen: silence, blank screen, torture_leave; with lives left it swaps the character set back and loads the next stage (stage_next), else game_restart.

Pays the reward, once the digit has been printed (the cell at $470B is no longer $FF) and each time the flowing colours bring dark grey ($0B) to the front of story_colours (every 40 frames): the digit at $ABF3 counts down from 6 to 0; at each step potion_add adds the worth of Clyde's last potion pickup (the ADC operand at $B8B4, 1 or 5) to the kind award_kinds names and to the total. With the usual 1 that is six potions, two of each kind.
Operand of the LDY at $A003: the new digit (5 down to 0), the index into award_kinds.
For each step of potion_award (digit 0-5), the potion counter it pays into: 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3.
rescue_screen's count before the big text appears: set to $78 and counted down every other frame.

The first of twenty colours that flow along the big WELL DONE, red at the start: rescue_screen rotates the list a place every other frame, the last ($A02E) moving to the front, and this front colour goes to both rows of the big letters ($D883 and $D8AB, eighteen cells each) and the digit's top left cell ($DB0B).
The list's second colour (light red at the start), the big digit's top right cell ($DB0C).
The list's third colour (yellow at the start), the digit's bottom right cell ($DB34).

The list's fourth colour on, the first of them the digit's bottom left cell ($DB33). From the start: light red, red, blue, light blue, cyan, light blue, blue, brown, orange, light red, orange, brown, dark grey, green, light green, green.
The list's last colour, dark grey at the start, which moves to the front at each rotation.
The first of twenty colours that flow down the six story lines, white at the start: it colours the first line ($D91F, 26 cells), and potion_award pays each time it is dark grey ($0B).
The second colour, the second line ($D947, 26 cells).
The third colour, the third line ($D9BC, 35 cells).
The fourth colour, the fourth line ($D9E3, 35 cells).
The fifth colour, the fifth line ($DA5A, 37 cells).
The sixth colour on, the first of them the sixth line ($DA82, 37 cells). From the start: light green, cyan, green, dark grey, black, black, brown, orange, light red, yellow, then white.
The list's last colour, white at the start, moved to the front at each rotation.

The sign's fade step, counted down from 7 to 0 every other frame by raster_rescue_top and indexing matrix_colours, matrix_mc1 and matrix_mc2: matrix_scroll sets it to 7 six frames before each letter changes, so the dots have faded to black, or nearly, when it does.
The sign's sprite colour for each fade step 0-7: light red when settled, then orange, brown, black at steps 3-5, brown and orange.
The sign's first sprite multicolour for each fade step 0-7: dark grey when settled, black at steps 1-7.
